audit.whatIsWrong: The shield is attributed to Purge in two places: spikes[0] "Purge (W) shreds you while he shields" and early "Purge out-DPSes your Unstable Matter while shielding", plus whys[2] "his shield uptime and sustained damage".
audit.why: Purge has no shield. The shield is on Disdain (E) — "Urgot charges in a direction, shielding himself". This sends the player to bait the wrong spell: Purge at max rank has a 0-second cooldown and can never be waited out, while Disdain is 16 seconds at rank 1 and is the actual bait target.
audit.corrected: Shield re-attributed to Disdain in spikes[0], early and whys[2].
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (W Purge — slow only; E Disdain — shield, hardCC)

audit.whatIsWrong: Disdain is never mentioned anywhere in the content layer — not in whys, spikes, early, mid or late.
audit.why: It is the ability that decides the matchup. Zac commits with a single telegraphed slingshot; Disdain catches him, stops, and hurls him out of the way, cancelling the engage outright. The full layer already names it matchup-defining, so the content layer is silent on the one cooldown the full layer says to track. This is the largest gap in the entry.
audit.corrected: Added to whys[2], mid, early and breakdown.cooldowns as the engage gate, with the 16s rank-1 figure.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] ends "his execute scales off your missing health".
audit.why: Fear Beyond Death impales, and if the target then falls below a health threshold Urgot may recast to execute. It is a binary threshold, not a missing-health damage scale. The practical difference is real: a Zac at 40% is in no more danger from the execute than a Zac at 90%, so the rule is "never dip under the line", not "never fight while hurt".
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (R Fear Beyond Death: "If that champion falls below a health threshold ... can execute them")

audit.whatIsWrong: Purge is described purely as a threat; nothing notes what it costs Urgot to use.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Urgot slows himself while he unloads his weapon on nearby enemies." He cannot chase or disengage during it, and its range is only 490. That is a genuine window for a knock-up engage rather than a reason to stay away, and it is the opposite of how the entry reads.
audit.corrected: Added to whys[1], spikes[0] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content level chart gives Urgot 6 of 7 stages against a win rate of exactly 50.00%; the full layer gives Zac four.
audit.why: A dead-even matchup charted 6-1 in one layer and 4-2 the other way in the other.
audit.corrected: Content chart set to Urgot/Skill/Zac/Zac/Urgot/Urgot/Zac — three stages each. Urgot keeps level 1, level 6 and the first-item spike the existing prose argues for.

audit.why: Corrosive Charge causing Purge to prioritise the struck target is already correctly described as "slows for a free follow-up", matching Riot's "Prioritizes enemy champions Urgot has recently struck with other abilities". Left alone.

edits.before: His Q slow into leg autos keeps beating you at L2.
edits.after: At 2 Purge slows Urgot too, so he can't chase you.

edits.before: At 3 his shield uptime and sustained damage still out-trade you.
edits.after: At 3 your E-Q-W lands if Disdain is down — that is the gate.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 his DPS pattern out-duels your burst.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 blobs outlast his sustained leg DPS.

edits.before: Urgot's Purge (W) shreds you while he shields, and Corrosive Charge (Q) slows for a free follow-up — don't Slingshot in for a W trade, his sustained DPS beats your burst in melee range.
edits.after: Urgot's Purge (W) shreds you inside 490 range and Corrosive Charge (Q) slows so Purge locks onto you — but the shield is Disdain (E), not W, and Purge slows Urgot himself while it runs.

edits.before: Fear Beyond Death (R) executes you below the health threshold and flips you if you're low, so as a big-health tank you must never dive him at 6 without a clear lead — his execute scales off your missing health.
edits.after: Fear Beyond Death (R) impales you, and if you then drop under the health threshold he can recast to execute. It is a threshold, not missing-health scaling — so the danger is dipping under the line at all, not how hurt you are.

edits.before: Urgot bullies you 1-3: Purge out-DPSes your Unstable Matter while shielding, and Corrosive Charge slows you into free autos, so respect his range and don't W-trade into his shield.
edits.after: Urgot bullies you at 1: Purge out-DPSes your W inside 490 range and Corrosive Charge slows you into it. The shield is Disdain (E) — that is the cooldown to bait, not Purge.

edits.before: Through 6 his kit only gets scarier — the R execute is lethal to a low tank and his shield-DPS pattern beats you 1v1, so farm patiently, ward for his slow ganks, and look to scale rather than solo-kill.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are yours when Disdain is down — a 16s rank-1 flip that cancels your slingshot, so bait it, then commit. From 6 the R execute punishes any dip under the threshold, so bank blobs before you dive.

edits.before: - Urgot Disdain: matchup-defining — His engage. E-knock after it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Urgot Disdain: matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1, shields him and flips you out of your own engage. Bait it, then commit. - Purge: slows Urgot while it runs, so he cannot chase. - Your E: 21s at rank 1, not for chip.

notes: DO NOT APPLY the _missing-interactions.json entry for this matchup: "Your Elastic Slingshot (E) shuts off Urgot's Corrosive Charge (Q) — hold it for the engage, not the poke." Both halves are wrong. Zac's E carries a spurious "grounding" flag in champ-data/_kits/zac.json, almost certainly derived from the word "ground" in Riot's text ("attaches his arms to the ground"); Elastic Slingshot applies no grounding. And Urgot's Q carries a spurious "dash" flag despite Corrosive Charge being a ground-targeted explosive with no dash component. Nothing in the kit supports the interaction, so I did not write it. The same bogus "grounding" flag on Zac's E is likely generating similar false interactions for other Zac matchups across the dataset — worth a sweep.
